findingDetails.title: The refusal and question rows can still carry a command, and no gate consumes the count
findingDetails.scopeProof: The fit continue removes the rows before the false_offer tally; the slice test only checks carried <= total; the baseline records 8 of 24; the bridge mutating field is never read.
findingDetails.claim: The 24 decline rows are removed before the false-offer tally and their carried count is only checked against itself, so a refusal or question that carries a command cannot fail any test or gate; the committed baseline records 8 of 24.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the fit rows are included in false_offer (not); whether the slice test compares carried to the baseline (no; only <= total); whether the handler guard should keep carried at 0 (baseline captured after the fix still records 8); whether the 8 are read-only (the tally never reads mutating; 26 of 63 bridge entries are mutates).
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The fit block may be an advisory measurement of handler quality rather than a release gate, and the 8 may be commands the handler intentionally offers on those row kinds.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the packet decision record says the fit block is advisory-only and the 8 are accepted, downgrade to P2 and record it as an accepted risk; if a test or gate is added that fails on carried > baseline, the finding resolves.

findingDetails.title: The holdout publication guard reads the baseline, not the live capture
findingDetails.scopeProof: publishRow is the only publication gate; the live row comparison filters holdout ids; the only live holdout check is the fit- prefix filter.
